overall_summary: Bitcoin faces heavy pressure after sliding to multi-year lows, with large ETF outflows and long liquidations adding to the selloff. Sticky inflation talk and fresh geopolitical flashpoints are keeping risk appetite weak. Near-term tone stays cautious ahead of key inflation and growth data.
key_points: BTC near two-year lows with heavy long liquidations
Spot Bitcoin ETFs see large outflows
Miner stress as price sits below estimated costs
Rate-hike rhetoric and risk-off macro backdrop
Geopolitical escalation risks across multiple theaters

items.title: Bitcoin Crashes to Two-Year Low Near $55K-$57K
items.summary: Bitcoin slid below sixty thousand for the first time since July and printed lows around fifty-five to fifty-seven thousand, its weakest levels in roughly two years. The drop came as AI and tech stocks sold off hard after Anthropic's rocky Nasdaq debut and broader valuation fears, pulling risk assets lower. Traders should care because this broke key summer supports, erased the prior rebound, and leaves the market testing whether this is capitulation or the start of deeper bear-market lows. Extreme fear readings and heavy volume confirm the move is not noise.
items.impact: Sustained downside pressure and risk of further support tests

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Shed $582M, Biggest Day in Weeks
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about five hundred eighty-two million dollars in net outflows on Thursday, the largest single day since late October, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for roughly five hundred forty-one million. November outflows are approaching three and a half billion dollars and total fund assets have shrunk. This matters because ETF flows are the cleanest gauge of institutional demand; sustained redemptions force actual Bitcoin selling and remove a key bid that supported prior rallies. Friday saw additional outflows continuing the trend.
items.impact: Removes institutional bid and adds direct selling pressure

items.title: Crypto Liquidations Top $1B-Plus, Mostly Longs
items.summary: Leveraged crypto positions saw between one and one-point-five billion dollars liquidated over twenty-four hours, with longs making up the vast majority, often over eighty-five or ninety percent. Bitcoin alone accounted for hundreds of millions in forced closes as price flushed lower. Traders need to watch this because cascading liquidations amplify moves, wipe out over-levered bulls, and can create temporary oversold conditions, but they also leave the book cleaner for the next directional move once the flush ends.
items.impact: Amplifies downside via forced selling; potential short-term washout

items.title: JPMorgan: BTC Far Below $86K Mining Cost, Miners Pressured
items.summary: JPMorgan analysts put Bitcoin's estimated average production cost near eighty-six thousand dollars. With spot price under sixty thousand the gap has widened past twenty-six thousand, and they say higher-cost miners are likely selling reserves to stay afloat or fund shifts into AI. This is important for traders because miner selling adds persistent supply overhang, and any hashrate drop or difficulty adjustment could eventually help, but near-term it reinforces bearish flow. The bank also noted retail driving most ETF outflows while institutional futures positioning held better.
items.impact: Adds miner selling supply and overhang on rallies

items.title: Binance Hackers Mix $149M BTC Through Coinjoins
items.summary: Blockchain firm Elliptic reports that wallets linked to the massive October Binance hack have pushed at least two thousand three hundred ten Bitcoin, worth about one hundred forty-nine million dollars, through coinjoin mixers, with roughly ninety percent of that activity since mid-week. The mixed coins came mostly from swapped stolen ETH and other assets rather than the original untouched Binance Bitcoin haul. Traders should note this because accelerated laundering raises the chance of eventual cash-outs or OTC dumps that can hit liquidity, while also keeping regulatory and exchange-risk headlines alive.
items.impact: Potential future selling pressure and lingering exchange-risk overhang

items.title: Bitcoin Core Patches AI-Found Node-Stall Bug
items.summary: Bitcoin Core released versions thirty-point-five and thirty-one-point-three fixing a medium-severity bug, CVE-twenty twenty-six-one one seven three four eight, that let a peer stall a node by repeating one orphan transaction ID fifty thousand times. The flaw was discovered by an AI scanner called Loupe from Block's Spiral unit. While not an immediate price catalyst, it matters because node stability underpins the network; rapid disclosure and patching reduce operational risk for exchanges, miners, and infrastructure, and show AI tools are now finding real Bitcoin code issues.
items.impact: Positive for network resilience, limited near-term price effect

items.title: Fed's Cook Pushes More Rate Hikes on Sticky Inflation
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said Friday the current policy rate is not high enough and more hikes are needed, calling inflation a great concern after 67 months above target. She reiterated her October dissent, warning that waiting risks falling behind the curve and forcing larger later moves. Crypto traders should care because hawkish Fed speak keeps December hike odds elevated and pressures risk assets via higher discount rates and tighter liquidity.
items.impact: Supports higher rates and stronger dollar, weighing on Bitcoin and equities

items.title: UMich Sentiment Rises to 51.5 as Inflation Expectations Cool
items.summary: The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for November came in at 51.5, up from 48.0 in October and slightly above the preliminary 51.0. One-year inflation expectations plunged to 3.7 percent from 4.7 percent, while five-to-ten year views eased to 3.3 percent. Traders should note the drop in inflation expectations could ease some Fed pressure if sustained, though the absolute level remains historically weak and post-election partisan shifts played a role.
items.impact: Mildly supportive via cooler inflation views but sentiment still subdued

items.title: Treasury Yields Plunge on Risk-Off Flight to Safety
items.summary: The US 10-year yield fell more than 10 basis points Friday to around 4.91 percent, its largest daily drop in a month, with the 2-year also sliding sharply. The move came as tech stocks sold off hard and investors sought bonds for safety rather than pure rate-cut hopes. Crypto desks watch this closely because falling yields can ease valuation pressure on risk assets, but the risk-off driver and still-elevated absolute levels keep the signal mixed ahead of next week's data.
items.impact: Lower yields potentially supportive short-term but risk-off tone dominates

items.title: Dollar Eases After Hitting 19-Month Highs
items.summary: The US dollar index slipped slightly Friday after touching multi-month peaks near 104, ending around 103.8 as Treasury yields fell and the multi-session rally stalled. Safe-haven flows limited the downside even as risk appetite waned. For crypto traders a softer DXY removes one headwind, but the dollar remains elevated on Fed hike bets and any rebound would quickly pressure Bitcoin again.
items.impact: Slight relief for risk assets if the stall continues

items.title: Core PCE and GDP Second Estimate Due Wednesday
items.summary: Markets head into a data-heavy Wednesday November 25 with the second estimate of Q3 GDP and the Fed's preferred Core PCE inflation gauge for October, both at 8:30 ET, plus personal income and spending. Prior GDP was 3.4 percent annualized and Core PCE around 3.1 percent year-over-year. This is the key inflation print before the December FOMC, so any upside surprise would reinforce hike bets and hit crypto hard while a cool print could spark a relief bounce.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst that will reset Fed path expectations

items.title: Fed Balance Sheet Edges Lower as Net Liquidity Holds
items.summary: The latest weekly Fed H.4.1 showed total assets around 6.74 trillion dollars, slightly lower on the week, with net liquidity estimates near 5.85 trillion after accounting for the TGA and reverse repo. Reserves remain ample near 3 trillion. Liquidity watchers track this for any tightening impulse that could drain market funding and pressure leveraged crypto positions, though changes remain gradual for now.
items.impact: Stable liquidity backdrop with no fresh squeeze signal

items.title: Trump Weighs New Iran Strikes as Military Warns of Strain
items.summary: Hawkish officials in Washington and Israel are pressing President Trump to resume major strikes on Iran, while US Central Command warns that prolonged deployments risk eroding readiness if the conflict drags into the new year. Trump has said he is not rushing and will decide after January, even as diplomacy stalls and energy markets stay on edge. Traders should watch this closely because any fresh escalation would hit oil supply through Hormuz and drive risk-off moves across crypto and equities.
items.impact: Heightens oil spike and risk-off volatility for Bitcoin

items.title: Russian Missiles and Drone Hit Poland Near NATO Drills
items.summary: Two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in southeastern Poland during a massive overnight barrage on Ukraine, with no injuries reported. Polish leaders called it an intentional provocation timed near European military exercises, and NATO labeled it a grave airspace violation. This raises the stakes for alliance response and could spill into broader European risk premium that hits risk assets.
items.impact: NATO tension spikes risk-off pressure on crypto

items.title: Iran Downs US Drones Over Hormuz as Talks Stall
items.summary: Iran's IRGC claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 and an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, marking dozens of such incidents since the war began. Diplomacy remains deadlocked as Iran demands sanctions relief and an end to the blockade before reopening the strait, while the US added new sanctions on Iranian oil intermediaries. Ongoing shipping threats keep a geopolitical premium in energy and favor defensive positioning in markets.
items.impact: Sustains Hormuz disruption risk and energy volatility

items.title: Houthis Fire Missiles at Riyadh After Tower Strike
items.summary: Saudi-led forces intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh early Saturday, the second attack on the capital in days after a strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower. The Iran-aligned group vowed further hits on Saudi ports and energy sites following coalition operations in Yemen. Fresh attacks on the world's top oil exporter keep supply fears alive and support higher energy prices that can pressure risk assets.
items.impact: Adds oil supply risk premium from Gulf attacks

items.title: Trump Pushes Ukraine Peace Deal Before Democrats Take Congress
items.summary: The Trump administration is pressing for a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement by early January, before Democrats assume control of Congress after the midterms. Envoys Kushner and Witkoff are shuttling talks while Russia continues heavy drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. A rushed deal could reduce European war risk but also signal concessions that unsettle allies; markets will price the uncertainty until terms firm up.
items.impact: Unresolved peace timeline keeps geo premium mixed

items.title: Massive Russian Barrage Hits Ukraine After Crimea Bridge Strike
items.summary: Russia launched one of its heaviest attacks of the year with hundreds of drones and over a hundred missiles, killing civilians and damaging bridges and energy sites in Kyiv and beyond. The strikes followed Ukrainian hits on the Kerch Bridge and came as Trump claimed Putin wants a diplomatic end. Intensified air war keeps Ukrainian resilience and European energy security in focus for traders watching broader risk sentiment.
items.impact: Prolonged conflict supports defensive risk posture
